questions.question: A tap fills a cistern in 14 hours. Another tap empties the full tank in 18 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill the tank completely, if the tank is empty and both the taps are open together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Filling tap time = 14 hours

Emptying tap time = 18 hours

**Formula used:**

LCM method: Take LCM of both times to assume total work (litres)

Then: Work done per hour = Filling - Emptying

Time = Total work ÷ Net work per hour

**Calculation:**

⇒ LCM of 14 and 18 = 126 litres (assume total capacity)

⇒ Filling rate = 126 ÷ 14 = 9 litres/hour

⇒ Emptying rate = 126 ÷ 18 = 7 litres/hour

⇒ Net rate = 9 − 7 = 2 litres/hour

⇒ Time = 126 ÷ 2 = 63 hours

**∴ The tank will be filled completely in 63 hours.**

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 24 days and B can complete it in 28 days. If they work on alternate days, starting with B on the first day, then in how many days will the work be finished?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can complete work in 24 days

B can complete work in 28 days

They work on alternate days starting with B

**Formula used:**

LCM method: Assume total work = LCM of 24 and 28

Work per day = Total work ÷ Time

Alternate day work: Add work done by B and A alternately

**Calculation:**

⇒ LCM of 24 and 28 = 168 units (assume total work)

⇒ A's 1 day work = 168 ÷ 24 = 7 units

⇒ B's 1 day work = 168 ÷ 28 = 6 units

⇒ Work in 2 days (B + A) = 6 + 7 = 13 units

Now, total work = 168 units

⇒ 13 units done every 2 days

⇒ Work done in 12 full cycles (24 days) = 12 × 13 = 156 units

⇒ Remaining work = 168 − 156 = 12 units

⇒ Next day is B’s turn (since last was A)

⇒ B does 6 units on 25th day, remaining = 12 − 6 = 6 units

⇒ A does 7 units per day, but only 6 units needed

⇒ A will finish in 6 ÷ 7 = 6/7 day

⇒ Total days = 25 + 6/7 = 25⁶⁄₇ days

**∴ The work will be finished in 25⁶⁄₇ days**

questions.question: A tap fills a cistern in 9 hours. Another tap empties the full tank in 90 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill twice the volume of the tank, if the tank is empty initially and both the taps are open together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Tap A fills the tank in 9 hours

Tap B empties the full tank in 90 hours

We need to find the time to fill 2 tanks when both taps are open together

**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Total work / Time

**Calculation:**

Let the total work = LCM of 9 and 90 = 90 units 

Total work to fill twice the volume of the tank = 2 × 90 = 180 units

Efficiency of A = 90 ÷ 9 = 10 units/hour

Efficiency of B = 90 ÷ 90 = 1 unit/hour (emptying)

Net efficiency = 10 − 1 = 9 units/hour

⇒ Time = 180 ÷ 9 = 20 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 20 hours.**

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill an empty cistern in 21 minutes and 42 minutes, respectively. Both Pipe A and Pipe B are opened together. After how much time should Pipe B be turned off so that the empty cistern is completely filled in a total of 16 minutes?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A fills cistern in = 21 minutes

Pipe B fills cistern in = 42 minutes

Total time to fill cistern = 16 minutes

**Calculations:**

Total Capacity of the cistern = LCM (21, 42) = 42 units

Efficiency of Pipe A (EA) = 42/21 = 2 units/minute

Efficiency of Pipe B (EB) = 42/42 = 1 unit/minute

Let 'x' be the time (in minutes) after which Pipe B is turned off.

Since the cistern is completely filled in a total of 16 minutes, Pipe A worked for the entire 16 minutes (as it was not turned off).

Pipe B worked for 'x' minutes.

Work done by Pipe A = EA × 16 = 2 × 16 = 32 units

Work done by Pipe B = EB × x = 1 × x = x units

The sum of work done by both pipes equals the Total Capacity:

Work done by A + Work done by B = Total Capacity

⇒ 32 + x = 42

⇒ x = 42 - 32

⇒ x = 10 minutes

**∴ Pipe B should be turned off after 10 minutes.**

questions.question: A and B can complete a work in 11 days and 33 days, respectively. They started doing the work together, but after 3 days, B had to leave, and A completed the remaining work alone. The remaining work was completed in ______ days.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A completes work in = 11 days

B completes work in = 33 days

Days worked together = 3 days

**Calculations:**

Total Work = LCM (11, 33) = 33 units

Efficiency of A (EA) = 33 / 11 = 3 units/day

Efficiency of B (EB) = 33 / 33 = 1 unit/day

Combined Efficiency (EA₊B) = EA + EB

⇒ Combined Efficiency = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day

Work done in 3 days (by A and B) = Combined Efficiency × Days worked together

⇒ Work done = 4 × 3 = 12 units

Remaining Work = Total Work - Work done

⇒ Remaining Work = 33 - 12 = 21 units

Days A will take to complete the remaining work = Remaining Work / Efficiency of A

⇒ Days = 21 / 3

⇒ Days = 7 days

**Therefore, the remaining work was completed in 7 days.**

questions.question: A tap fills a cistern in 18 hours. Another tap empties the full tank in 19 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill one-third of the tank, if the tank is empty initially and both the taps are open together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by the filling tap to fill the cistern = 18 hours

Time taken by the emptying tap to empty the full tank = 19 hours

We need to find the time to fill one-third of the tank.

**Calculations:**

**Total Work Units (LCM)**

LCM of 18 and 19:

LCM(18, 19) = 18 times 19 = 342 units

So, let the total capacity of the tank be 342 units.

**Calculate Individual Efficiencies**

Efficiency of the filling tap = frac{{Total Work}}{{Time to fill}} = frac{342 { units}}{18 { hours}} = 19 units/hour

Efficiency of the emptying tap = frac{{Total Work}}{{Time to empty}} = frac{342 { units}}{19 { hours}} = 18 units/hour

**Calculate Net Efficiency (when both taps are open)**

Net filling rate = Efficiency of filling tap - Efficiency of emptying tap

Net filling rate = 19 units/hour - 18 units/hour = 1 unit/hour

**Calculate Time to Fill One-third of the Tank**

The work to be done is one-third of the tank's capacity.

Work to be done = (1)/(3) times Total Work Units

Work to be done = (1)/(3) times 342 units = 114 units

Time taken = frac{{Work to be done}}{{Net filling rate}}

Time taken = frac{114 { units}}{1 { unit/hour}} = 114 hours

**∴ It will take 114 hours to fill one-third of the tank if both taps are open together.**

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 14 days and B can complete it in 10 days. If they work on alternate days, starting with B on the first day, then in how many days will the work be finished?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can complete the work in 14 days.

B can complete the work in 10 days.

They work on alternate days, starting with B on the first day.

**Formula used:**

Total Work (units) = LCM of individual time taken

Efficiency (units/day) = Total Work / Time taken

**Calculations:**

LCM of 14 and 10 = 70 units (Let the total work be 70 units)

Efficiency of A = (70)/(14) = 5 units/day

Efficiency of B = (70)/(10) = 7 units/day

They work on alternate days, starting with B:

Day 1: B works = 7 units

Day 2: A works = 5 units

Work done in 2 days (1 cycle) = 7 + 5 = 12 units

Number of full cycles to complete the work:

Divide total work by work done in 1 cycle: (70)/(12) = 5 with a remainder of 10.

This means 5 full cycles (5 × 2 = 10 days) will complete 5 × 12 = 60 units of work.

Work remaining = 70 - 60 = 10 units

After 10 days, B will start the next cycle (Day 11).

Day 11: B works and completes 7 units.

Work remaining = 10 - 7 = 3 units

Now, A will work on Day 12.

Time taken by A to complete the remaining 3 units = (3)/(5) days

Total time taken to complete the work = Days from full cycles + Days for remaining work

Total time = 10 days (from 5 cycles) + 1 day (by B on Day 11) + (3)/(5) day (by A on Day 12)

Total time = 10 + 1 + (3)/(5)

Total time = 11(3)/(5) days

**∴ The work will be finished in 11(3)/(5) days.**

questions.question: A tap fills a cistern in 18 hours. Another tap empties the full tank in 24 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill three-fourth of the tank, if the tank is empty initially and both the taps are open together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Filling tap fills in 18 hours

Emptying tap empties in 24 hours

Initial tank is empty, need to fill 3/4 of the tank

**Formula used:**

Work = LCM of times taken

Efficiency = Work ÷ Time

Net efficiency = Filling – Emptying

Time = Work ÷ Net Efficiency

**Calculations:**

LCM of 18 and 24 = 72 units (assume total capacity)

Filling tap's efficiency = 72 ÷ 18 = 4 units/hr

Emptying tap's efficiency = 72 ÷ 24 = 3 units/hr

Net efficiency = 4 - 3 = 1 unit/hr

3/4 of tank = 72 × 3 ÷ 4 = 54 units

⇒ Time = 54 ÷ 1 = 54 hours

**∴ Time to fill 3/4 of the tank = 54 hours**

questions.question: Two taps can fill a cistern in 2 hours and 81 hours, respectively. A third tap can empty it in 81 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill the empty cistern, if all of the taps are opened together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Tap A fills in = 2 hours

Tap B fills in = 81 hours

Tap C empties in = 81 hours

**Formula used:**

Work per hour = 1 / Time

Time = Total work / Net work per hour

**Calculation:**

Total work = LCM of 2 and 81 = 162 units

⇒ Tap A fills = 162 ÷ 2 = 81 units/hour

⇒ Tap B fills = 162 ÷ 81 = 2 units/hour

⇒ Tap C empties = 162 ÷ 81 = 2 units/hour

Net work/hour = 81 + 2 - 2 = 81 units/hour

Time = 162 ÷ 81 = 2 hours

**∴ Required time = 2 hours**

questions.question: A tap fills a cistern in 15 hours. Another tap empties the full tank in 17 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill two-third of the tank, if the tank is empty initially and both the taps are open together?

Emptying tap does = 255 ÷ 17 = 15 units/hour

Time = 170 ÷ 2 = 85 hours

questions.question: Two taps can fill a cistern in 4 hours and 32 hours, respectively. A third tap can empty it in 4 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill one-fourth of the empty cistern, if all of them are opened together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two taps can fill a cistern in 4 hours and 32 hours, respectively.

A third tap can empty the cistern in 4 hours.

We need to find the time taken to fill one-fourth of the cistern when all taps are opened together.

**Formula Used:**

Work done in 1 hour = LCM of times / Individual time.

Net work done in 1 hour = Work by first tap + Work by second tap - Work by third tap (since it empties).

Time taken = Required work (fraction of the tank) / Net work done in 1 hour.

**Calculation:**

Work done by the first tap in 1 hour = 1/4.

Work done by the second tap in 1 hour = 1/32.

Work done by the third tap in 1 hour = 1/4 (negative, as it empties).

LCM of 4 and 32 = 32.

Net work done in 1 hour = (32/4) + (32/32) - (32/4).

Net work done in 1 hour = 8 + 1 - 8 = 1/32.

Time taken to fill one-fourth of the cistern = (1/4) / (1/32).

Time taken = 1/4 × 32/1.

Time taken = 8 hours.

**The time required to fill one-fourth of the empty cistern is 8 hours.**

⇒ Time taken = 191.11 minutes

questions.question: A, B and C alone can do a piece of work in 5, 55 and 66 days, respectively. They all started the work together, but A left after 4 days. In how many days was the whole work completed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A = 5 days, B = 55 days, C = 66 days

A left after 4 days

**Formula used:**

Total work = LCM(5,55,66)

Efficiency = Total work ÷ time (days)

Time = Work ÷ (sum of efficiencies of workers working)

**Calculations:**

⇒ LCM(5,55,66) = 330 (since 5 × 11 × 6 = 330)

⇒ Efficiency A = 330 ÷ 5 = 66 units/day

⇒ Efficiency B = 330 ÷ 55 = 6 units/day

⇒ Efficiency C = 330 ÷ 66 = 5 units/day

⇒ Work done in 4 days by A + B + C = (66 + 6 + 5) × 4 = 77 × 4 = 308 units

⇒ Remaining work = 330 - 308 = 22 units

⇒ B + C efficiency = 6 + 5 = 11 units/day

⇒ Time to finish = 22 ÷ 11 = 2 days

⇒ Total time = 4 + 2 = 6 days

**∴ Whole work completed in 6 days.**

questions.question: Ramesh can complete a piece of work alone in 16 days and Suresh can complete the same piece of work alone in 10 days. They started the work together, but Ramesh had to leave 4 days before the completion of the work. In how many days will the work get completed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ramesh = 16 days, Suresh = 10 days

Ramesh left 4 days before completion

**Formula used:**

Total work = LCM of individual times (take as total capacity)

Efficiency = Total work ÷ time (units/day)

Work done = (R efficiency × days R worked) + (S efficiency × days S worked)

**Calculations:**

⇒ LCM(16, 10) = 80 (total work = 80 units)

⇒ Efficiency of Ramesh = 80 ÷ 16 = 5 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of Suresh = 80 ÷ 10 = 8 units/day

⇒ Let total days = T. Ramesh works (T − 4) days, Suresh works T days.

⇒ 5 × (T − 4) + 8 × T = 80

⇒ 5T − 20 + 8T = 80

⇒ 13T = 100

⇒ T = 100 ÷ 13 = 7(9)/(13) { days}

**∴ Work completed in 7(9)/(13) { days}.**

Work in 1 day = 1 ÷ number of days

**Calculation:**

A's 1 day work = 36 ÷ 12 = 3 units

B's 1 day work = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 units

Work in 2 days = 2 × 5 = 10 units

Remaining work = 36 - 10 = 26 units

Time for B alone = 26 ÷ 2 = 13 days

⇒ Total days = 2 + 13 = 15

**∴ The work was completed in 15 days.**
